Continued weakness in the market could prompt more shorts as these investors look to profit on the downward move. **_However:_** once they believe a ‘bottom’ has been found, these investors will ‘buy back’ these short positions which could inflate any rallies. • **Macro-Hedge funds** have likely reduced their long positions, as copper demand continues to underperform expectations, and the medium-term outlook for commodities in general has become less attractive as an investment given global economic uncertainty. However, this is an allocation decision. Yesterday’s statement from the Fed underscored the agency’s inability to do much to stimulate the US economy, leaving its fate to the politicians. That’s not very confidence-inspiring in itself, and the effect of **that was a huge sell** - **off in risk** - **related assets** , **such as equities and commodities** . • Until the EU has hit “rock bottom” with regard to its options on Greece, the markets will not expect the euro to strengthen. So, we are likely to see price weakness persist until a realistic, credible and definitive solution to Europe’s financial problems has been found. That could take some time. • In terms of the global economy, negative sentiment is not good for business confidence. We have already begun to see a pull-back in investment in the US, and Europe is likely to experience the same thing, given downside risks to the financial sector at this point. Given the latest data, China does not look **likely to be able to add a lot of momentum to the global manufacturing sector** . **Thus** , **it looks as though** global growth will be moving into low gear for the next couple of quarters. 3 Daily VIX "Fear Index" & LME 3-Mo Copper 11/03/2011 - 29/09/2011 (CHG)
